references.text: Prohibits moving a neighbor's boundary marker, which the ancestors established. This is the original legislation on which the curse in Deut 27:17 is based.
Warns against moving ancient boundary markers, showing that this was an important principle in Israel's legal practice.
Urges not to move boundary markers or encroach on the land of the fatherless, linking this to God's protection of the weak.
Notes that the wicked move boundary markers and steal livestock, as an example of evil.
The prophet compares Judah's leaders to those who move boundary markers and warns that the Lord's wrath will strike them.
A fundamental command to love your neighbor as yourself, which is the underlying principle behind the prohibition against violating a neighbor's property.
